conviction_note: Scale is the name's own median reaction (12.7%, no usable chain) nudged to 13 because a guide change is plausible; p_up 45 because the one company-level lever that can move the guide (the FY27 guide assumed tariffs turn into a tailwind, and the US-Canada cross-border tariff wall went up after the quarter closed) leans negative, while a low, semi-sourced Q2 bar ($0.63 against a $0.98 prior year the company only said would be 'lower'), a record Services backlog and a beat-and-reaffirm reaction history (+15.2%, +7.6%) pull back toward 50; the stock is already 27.7% off its high, so much of the macro is in the price.
bar: Q2 FY27 consensus adjusted EPS $0.63 / revenue $359.5M (MarketBeat, 2026-09-29, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-apogee-enterprises-apog-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/; Defense World repeats the same MarketBeat feed, so effectively one source). Company guide: FY27 adjusted EPS $2.70-$3.25, net sales $1.43-$1.48B with Kalwall; Q2 described qualitatively as net sales 'slightly lower' and adjusted EPS 'lower' year on year (prior year $358.2M / $0.98). The quarterly bar is single-sourced, so the findings that depend on it are sized small.
positioning_check: Short interest 4.91% of float, 4.34 days to cover as of the 2026-09-11 settlement (search snippet from Nasdaq's short-interest page https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/apog/short-interest; the page returned 503 on fetch, so this is snippet_only). findings.finding: The FY27 guide treated tariffs as a tailwind. On the Q4 FY26 call the CFO put FY26's tariff cost at about $9M, mostly from moving product across the Canada border and back, and said that cost 'will be a tailwind now in 27' with no new tariffs assumed. After Q2 closed (about 2026-08-29), the US put a 50% Section 338 tariff on Canadian goods (effective 2026-08-22), the Canada trade talks collapsed, Canada put 50% surtaxes on more than 300 US steel and aluminum products (effective 2026-09-08), and from 2026-09-15 the stacked rate on Canadian downstream aluminum products reached about 100%. That hits exactly the cross-border flow behind the $9M (Alumicor in Canada, US Metals plants) during the H2 the guide relies on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-cut prints were sold hard: 2026-01-07 -13.89%, 2025-04-23 -12.72%, 2025-01-07 -19.02% (baseline). A reaffirmed guide with a beat was bought +15.16% on 2026-06-26.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews quoted in the wire copy (MarketBeat 09-29, Investing.com) cite aluminum cost and market softness as risks and do not mention Section 338 or the cross-border tariff the guide booked as a tailwind. If the market had priced a guide cut, the stock would be marked down toward the January-2026 cut-reaction level and consensus FY EPS would sit below the $2.98 guide midpoint. The 27.7% drawdown since the June high says part of this is in the price, which is why p_up is only 45.
findings.independence: The policy facts come from a different source than the company figure: Manufacturing Dive 2026-08-26 (https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/canada-targets-us-steel-aluminum-retaliatory-tariffs-september-2026/828812/) and Discovery Alert on the 100% stack from 09-15 (https://discoveryalert.com/analysis/us-canada-aluminum-tariffs-september-2026/). The transmission to Apogee's P&L is an inference: the company has not quantified the new tariffs, and a 100% wall on Canadian downstream aluminum may also shield Apogee's US fabrication from Canadian competitors (CPA, https://prosperousamerica.org/cpa-applauds-administrations-increased-tariffs-for-american-aluminum-fabricators/). That is why the range is wide and this sets p_up at 45 rather than lower.

findings.finding: Aluminum costs ran at record highs through Apogee's June-August Q2. The US Midwest premium was at successive records above $1/lb until the September contract fell 8.2% to 95c/lb on 2026-08-21, which was after most of the quarter had passed. A direct architectural-glass and aluminum peer, Tecnoglass, reported Q2 CY26 adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.5% against 31.2% a year earlier, largely on aluminum. Apogee's Metals segment buys aluminum billet and extrusions and offsets it with surcharges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27, Metals margin rose to 11.2% from 7.3% despite higher aluminum, and the print was bought +15.16%. So this name has absorbed aluminum through surcharges before.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Management already guided Q2 EPS lower year on year, and consensus at $0.63 sits 36% below the prior year's $0.98. Only the size of the margin hit is open. That is why this is small.
findings.independence: Tecnoglass Q2 2026 release, a different source (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/06/3340090/0/en/tecnoglass-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-including-record-revenues-on-continued-market-share-gains.html). It is a peer read, and Apogee prices through surcharges, so it lands inside what the company already guided.

findings.finding: The H2 weighting of the guide rests on 'anticipated improvement in underlying market conditions'. The broad series has not improved: the AIA/Deltek Architecture Billings Index read 47.2 in August 2026 (46.6 in July), almost four years in contraction, the longest slump on record, and AIA's economist pointed to the Fed's latest rate increase as a further near-term headwind for project financing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the same guide line as the first finding. Guide cuts were sold -12.7% to -19.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The ABI is public and broad, so this is largely in the price. What is open is whether management keeps the second-half recovery assumption. Architectural Services backlog was a record $734.5M at Q1 and offsets this for one segment.
findings.independence: This is a macro proxy, not company-confirmed. Steel Market Update reported the same contraction (https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/09/24/aia-says-architecture-billings-remain-in-contraction/), but from the same AIA release, so it counts once.

findings.finding: The Q2 bar looks low against what the company has said. Consensus $0.63 / $359.5M compares with a Q1 beat of $0.57 against $0.43 (and $342.7M against $333.8M). Management described Q2 only as sales 'slightly lower' and EPS 'lower' than $358.2M / $0.98. Kalwall (about $85M a year, closed 2026-07-01) adds roughly two months, about $14M, inside Q2. Architectural Services has grown nine quarters running, and its backlog was a record $734.5M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-reaffirm prints were bought: +15.16% on 2026-06-26 and +7.59% on 2026-04-24.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly unpriced. The consensus ($0.63) is far below the prior year, and the stock fell 27% after a beat. If the market expected another clear beat, the stock would not be drifting down into the print (-3.8% over 5d). The bar comes from a single estimate source, so the weight stays small.
findings.independence: Q2 commentary from the Q1 call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/26/apogee-apog-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/), Kalwall terms from the 2026-07-01 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000068/ex991.htm), and the consensus from MarketBeat. These are three different documents.

findings.finding: Apogee signed (2026-09-02) and closed (2026-09-18) a second acquisition within the quarter: GroGlass, Riga, up to EUR 62.5M including EUR 10M earn-out, about $30M revenue at about 25% adjusted EBITDA margin, paid from cash and the revolver after Kalwall's $105M. Leverage was 1.3x before Kalwall. The money buys a business with a higher margin than Performance Surfaces.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print that turned on M&A. The Kalwall announcement and the reaffirmed guide coincided with the +15.16% June print.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public. What is not public is whether management, which committed debt mid-quarter knowing how Q2 went, will update guidance to include GroGlass. If the market read the deal as a confidence signal, the stock would not have fallen from about $37.9 (09-11) to $35.37.
findings.independence: The announcement 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000087/ex991-apogacquisitionann.htm) is the same company as the source. Reading the deal as a confidence signal is an inference, so it is sized small.
